answer: Reputation Decay Ledger: each identity carries a public score that decays exponentially when its actions go unchallenged; low-score accounts must post collateral before transacting. An attacker cloning identities pays full collateral on every clone, and each clone's decay restarts on a separate willow branch of the ledger, so splitting activity multiplies locked capital linearly. Clones confined to a small island of interactions decay fastest, forcing repeated top-ups. An honest account pays once and earns umber discounts as its score compounds.
